property_summary: For any bytes4 interfaceId input, supportsInterface MUST return true for IERC1155 and IERC1155MetadataURI; the bug returns false for those because it checks only IERC165.

For any bytes4 input, if the reference contract's supportsInterface returns true, then the buggy version must also return true (the reference's return value implies the bug's return value), but the bug breaks this because by only checking IERC165 it may return false when the reference returns true for IERC1155 or IERC1155MetadataURI.

For any bytes4 input, supportsInterface in the reference returns true exactly when the input matches IERC1155, IERC1155MetadataURI, or IERC165; the bug returns true only for IERC165, so there exists an input for which the reference returns true but the bug returns false.

For any bytes4 interfaceId, if the reference contract's supportsInterface returns true, then the buggy version must also return true (the reference's return value implies the bug's return value), but the bug breaks this because by only checking IERC165 it may return false when the reference returns true for IERC1155 or IERC1155MetadataURI.

For any bytes4 interfaceId, supportsInterface(interfaceId) must not revert and must return the same boolean value in both the reference and modified contracts; the bug violates this because it returns false for IERC1155 and IERC1155MetadataURI where the reference returns true.

interfaceId == type(IERC1155MetadataURI).interfaceId is always false in both versions and interfaceId == type(IERC1155).interfaceId is true in both, but the reference returns true for IERC1155MetadataURI's interfaceId while the bug returns false because super.supportsInterface(interfaceId) returns false for it.
For any interfaceId, supportsInterface should return true for IERC1155MetadataURI's interface ID in the reference, but the bug returns false because it only checks IERC1155 and ERC165.

For any valid ERC165 interface ID, the reference contract correctly reports support for IERC1155MetadataURI if and only if it matches type(IERC1155MetadataURI).interfaceId or super.supportsInterface returns true, while the buggy version fails to recognize IERC1155MetadataURI because it only checks IERC1155 and ERC165, returning false for an interface it should support.
For any input interfaceId, the reference contract reports true for the IERC1155MetadataURI interface ID while the buggy mutant falsely returns false.

For any bytes4 interfaceId, the contract's supportsInterface must return the same boolean as the logical OR of interfaceId equalling type(IERC1155).interfaceId, type(IERC1155MetadataURI).interfaceId, or the result of ERC165.supportsInterface(interfaceId); the mutant breaks this by omitting the IERC1155MetadataURI check, causing it to return false for that specific interface ID where the reference returns true.

For any admissible interfaceId, c.supportsInterface(interfaceId) must return true when interfaceId equals type(IERC1155).interfaceId (0xd9b67a26); the buggy version returns false because it only checks for IERC1155MetadataURI.
For the correct contract, supportsInterface must return true when given the IERC1155 interface ID, but the buggy version returns false for that ID because it only checks for IERC1155MetadataURI.

For every bytes4 interfaceId, c.supportsInterface(interfaceId) must return the same value as would be returned by an ERC165 implementation that supports both IERC1155 and IERC1155MetadataURI; the mutant violates this by never returning true for IERC1155's interface id (0xd9b67a26).
For any bytes4 interfaceId, the correct contract returns true when interfaceId equals the IERC1155 interface identifier, but the mutant returns false for that identifier.

For every bytes4 interfaceId, the correct contract supports both IERC1155 and IERC1155MetadataURI interfaces while the mutant only supports IERC1155MetadataURI, so there exists some interfaceId for which the correct contract returns true and the mutant returns false.

For any interfaceId, supportsInterface in the reference also returns true for type(ERC165).interfaceId (via super), while the mutant never does; the fuzzer can pick type(ERC165).interfaceId to find a return mismatch.

For any bytes4 interfaceId, the reference contract's supportsInterface returns true for type(IAccessControl).interfaceId due to inherited ERC165, but the mutant's supportsInterface returns false since it omits the super call, violating the ERC165 inheritance requirement.

For any interfaceId, the reference C's supportsInterface correctly returns true for type(IERC165).interfaceId due to inherited ERC165, but the mutant's supportsInterface returns false because it omits the super.supportsInterface call, thus breaking the ERC165 requirement that supportsInterface(type(IERC165).interfaceId) must be true.
For any bytes4 interfaceId, supportsInterface must return true if the interfaceId is type(IERC165).interfaceId (inherited via ERC165), which the mutant violates by omitting the super call.

For any bytes4 interfaceId, the reference contract's supportsInterface returns true for type(ERC165).interfaceId due to the super call, but the mutant returns false because it omits the super chain, violating the ERC165 standard.
balanceOf returns the correct balance for any account, including address(0), and the bug version removes the revert for address(0) thus returns a value instead of reverting.
For any non-zero address and any token ID, calling balanceOf should return the actual minted/burnt balance, not a constant 0 as the mutant does.
For any user that has minted some quantity of a token, balanceOf(user, tokenId) must equal the minted amount; the mutant returns 0 instead.
For any address and token ID where tokens have been minted, balanceOf must return the actual balance, not zero.
For any address and token ID after minting that token to that address, c.balanceOf(account, id) must return the minted amount; the mutant always returns 0.
After a successful mint or transfer to an address, balanceOf must return the total minted amount plus any transferred amount; the mutant always returns 0 regardless of mints or transfers.
balanceOf for any token id must return the balance stored for that id; the mutant returns the balance for id+1, so for any id, calling balanceOf with id incorrectly reads the balance of id+1.

For any token ID, balanceOf must return the balance of the requested ID, not the balance of a different ID; the mutant incorrectly returns the balance of id+1, so calling balanceOf for id max returns the balance for a non-existent id, potentially reading uninitialized storage, whereas the correct contract returns the balance of id max itself.

For any token id, calling balanceOf returns the balance stored for that exact id; the mutant returns the balance for id+1, so for any minted token id the returned balance will not match the actual balance of that id.

The balanceOf function must return the actual token balance stored in _balances, but the mutant always inflates the returned value by 1, violating the property that balanceOf returns exactly the stored balance.

balanceOf must return an amount that, when added to another account's balance for the same token, does not exceed total supply implicit from mint events, but the mutant adds 1 making sums exceed real totals.

The balanceOf view returns the actual token holdings, not the type(uint256).max constant, for any valid account and token ID; the bug breaks this for all non-zero balances by returning the maximum possible value.

For any valid accounts and token IDs that have been minted, calling balanceOfBatch(accounts, ids) must return non-zero balances for at least one account-token pair when the corresponding individual balanceOf calls are non-zero, but the buggy version violates this by always returning zero.
For two arbitrary length-matched account/ID arrays, the balanceOfBatch array view must match the per-element balanceOf calls; the bug breaks by returning all zeros regardless of actual holdings.
For any accounts and IDs arrays, if the first element non-zero-addr has positive balance, balanceOfBatch must return the same positive value; bug returns zero.

For any pair of equal-length account and ID arrays, if balanceOfBatch returns successfully, each element must equal the corresponding individual balanceOf call; the bug breaks this by always returning zero.

For any equal-length arrays of accounts and ids where every account is the zero address, balanceOfBatch must return an array of all zeros; the bug also returns all zeros, so it can't be distinguished. For any non-zero account with a non-zero balance at an id, the bug returns zero, violating the rule that balanceOfBatch[i] equals the current balanceOf(accounts[i], ids[i]).

For any valid input arrays, balanceOfBatch must return the correct balance for every requested (account, id) pair; the buggy loop skips every other index, leaving those entries as zero and violating correctness for some inputs.

For any valid input arrays, the length of balanceOfBatch's returned array must equal the input arrays' length; the buggy loop leaves uninitialized slots, but the reference always returns exactly accounts.length elements.

For any valid input arrays of equal length, balanceOfBatch must return an array where the value at every even or odd index matches the balance of the corresponding (account, id) pair; the buggy loop only sets every other element (those at even indices) leaving odd-index entries zero, which violates the rule for some inputs.

For any valid equal-length address and uint256 arrays, balanceOfBatch returns an array where every element equals the balanceOf for the corresponding account and id; the buggy loop increments by 2, so all odd-indexed entries remain uninitialized as zero, breaking the property for inputs with length >= 2.

For any equal-length address and uint256 arrays, the returned batchBalances array must have its last element equal to the balanceOf of the corresponding last account and id; the buggy loop may skip setting the last element if the length is even, leaving it as zero.

For any call to balanceOfBatch with at least one element, the returned array must have the same declared length as the inputs, but the mutant returns an array where the last element is left as zero instead of the actual balance.
